prose: # The Brennan Bridge
The Brennan Bridge crosses the Tarrow river two miles north of Kilnagh.
Its engineer, Maud Ferris, designed the three stone arches after a flood took the ferry.
The bridge opened to traffic in 1937 and was widened in 1968.
# The Kilnagh orchard
The orchard behind the old mill grows eleven kinds of apple.
Its oldest tree is a russet planted by the miller's daughter.
Every October the village presses the fallen fruit into cider.
# The observatory on Carn Hill
A small observatory stands on the summit of Carn Hill.
Its brass telescope was bought second-hand from a college in Dublin.
On clear winter nights the volunteers open the dome to visitors.
# The Tarrow ferry
Before the bridge, a flat-bottomed ferry carried carts across the river.
The ferryman charged a penny a wheel and nothing for a walker.
The last crossing was made in the spring of 1936.
# The weaving school
The weaving school was founded by three sisters in an empty granary.
Its looms were built by a carpenter from the next valley.
The school still sells blankets dyed with heather and lichen.
# The river festival
Each July the town holds a festival of boats on the Tarrow.
Children race wooden boats they carved themselves.
The winner rings the bell on the bridge at sunset.
